description: We are Wekalet Fasa. We combine research, software development, and interactive storytelling to explore that question. In our demo, users follow an astronaut through a simulated mission and see how comparing readings with the astronaut’s usual patterns can help the crew decide what needs attention on board and what can wait for a review on Earth.
summary:
On a Mars mission a message to Earth takes 20+ minutes each way, so the crew has
to make the first health decisions on board. Orbital Signs compares every reading with the astronaut'sown baseline, catches bad readings before they raise a false alarm, and uses fixed, testable rules (not AI) to decide what needs action now and what can wait for Earth. A voice and text companion, Echo, explains the numbers in plain words, and every number it says is checked by code.
details:
Orbital Signs is a web app that works as a personal health companion for one astronaut. It has four ideas:

• Know your normal. Each reading is compared with the astronaut's own baseline, built from their last 14 days of readings, not with a population average.

• Catch bad readings first. Reading-quality checks (for example, blood pressure right after exercise) ask for a retake instead of raising an alarm.

• Rules decide, AI explains. What needs action on board and what can wait for Earth is decided only by named, tested rules. Every decision cites the rule that made it. AI is allowed to phrase an answer, never to decide one.

• Echo, a companion you can talk or type to. Ask about your numbers or NASA research in plain language; Echo answers from the astronaut's own data and NASA notes.
projectRefs: Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
